source_text: lta bona tacens de malo, contra quod pugnas: sed cum taces, clamas: "Parentes qui conventu suo causam fecere peccato, iure damnabiles; quorum labore actum est ut ad dominatum exercendum in homines diabolus perveniret
pass_a_gloss: Lta goods tacens about/from to-evil, against that/which pugnas: but when/with taces, secretly: " parents who conventu his-own case fecere by-sin, by-right worthy-of-condemnation; quorum labore done is so-that/as to dominatum exercendum in human-beings the-devil perveniret.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Through what is sin found in infants?
Parents who, through their union, supplied the cause of sin are rightly liable to condemnation. By their work they brought it about that the devil gained the power to rule over human beings.
The origin of those who are born comes from the devil, because the origin of sin, without which no human being is born, is said to come from the devil.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
